image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a black rectangular loudspeaker enclosure resting on a wooden surface. The speaker features a large central woofer with a metallic-looking cone and rubber surround, flanked by two smaller circular drivers (likely mid-range or tweeters) on the left side. There are visible mounting screws and a port opening at the bottom left. The finish appears to be matte black plastic or coated MDF.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is one large central cone and two smaller circular components on the left, all varying in size.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Prominent large woofer dominating the front face with a much smaller tweeter positioned above or beside it.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large woofer dominates the right/center area, and smaller drivers are positioned beside it on the left.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The drivers are exposed; there is no grille cloth or perforated metal covering them.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The reflection on the large woofer cone is unusually uniform and 'plastic-like,' lacking the subtle micro-texture often seen in real paper or polypropylene cones. It looks slightly like a rendered gradient rather than physical material reflection.

artifact_observations.location: Screws on the large woofer frame
artifact_observations.reasoning: The screws securing the woofer basket appear slightly malformed or fused into the frame. The heads lack distinct Phillips/slot details and look like vague indentations, a common AI artifact in small mechanical details.
The left edge of the speaker box seems to curve slightly inward or blend softly into the background shadow, rather than maintaining a strict straight geometric line expected of a rigid box.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of speaker and ensure it aligns with ImageNet class definitions despite the unusual driver layout.
To verify the rigidity of the box shape and check for edge bleeding or warping along the straight lines of the enclosure.
To closely inspect the texture of the cones and the mechanical integrity of the screws/mounting points for subtle generation artifacts.
To ensure the speaker sits correctly on the wooden surface without floating or incorrect shadow grounding.

focus_areas: Mechanical precision of screws and mounting hardware
Material texture realism of speaker cones (reflection patterns)
Geometric straightness of the enclosure edges
Logical consistency of driver arrangement (port placement vs drivers)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'screws' on the speaker frame. AI often fails to render distinct screw heads, resulting in melted or vague indentations. Also, evaluate if the reflection on the main woofer is physically plausible for a matte/cone surface, or if it exhibits the 'smooth gradient' artifact typical of diffusion models. Check if the port hole at the bottom left has a valid depth interior or if it looks like a flat black shape.
